after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Which of the matrices below are singular?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
- For the matrix $A$, we have

$$
det(A)=0\cdot 0-1\cdot 1=-1.
$$

Because $det(A)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $A$ is invertible.

- The matrix $B$ is a $3\times 1$ matrix. So, it is not invertible. Since the matrix is not square, we can't say that it's singular.

- For the matrix $C$, we have

$$
det(C)=1\cdot 0-0\cdot 1=0.
$$

Because $det(C)=0,$ we conclude that $C$ is not invertible. Since $C$ is a square matrix that is not invertible, we also say that $C$ is singular.

Therefore, only $C$ is singular.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: If $Q=[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ x & x\end{aligned}]$ is a singular matrix, calculate the value of $x.$
after.worked_solution:
The matrix $Q$ is singular if and only if $det(Q)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Q) & =3\cdot x-x\cdot 6 \\  & =3x-6x \\  & =-3x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x & =0 \\ x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of $x$ is $x=0.$

The matrix Q is singular if and only if det(Q)=0. Calculating the determinant, we get

det(Q)=3⋅x−x⋅6=3x−6x=−3x

Now, we set the determinant equal to 0 and solve for x:

−3x=0x=0

content.knowledge_point: Solving for a Variable in a Singular Matrix
content.problem: If $Q=[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ x & x\end{aligned}]$ is a singular matrix, calculate the value of $x.$
content.worked_solution:
The matrix $Q$ is singular if and only if $det(Q)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Q) & =3\cdot x-x\cdot 6 \\  & =3x-6x \\  & =-3x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x & =0 \\ x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of $x$ is $x=0.$

$$

\begin{aligned}det(B) & =(2x+4)\cdot (-x-3)-0\cdot 15 \\  & =-2{x}^{2}-6x-4x-12 \\  & =-2{x}^{2}-10x-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2}-10x-12 & =0 \\ -2({x}^{2}+5x+6) & =0 \\ (x+3)(x+2) & =0 \\ x & =-3,-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the values of $x$ are

$$
x=-3\,\text{and}\,x=-2.
$$
